Fight breaks out in women’s soccer win, fall 3-0 to Butte in following game

Nicholas Ramirez, Sports Editor
November 10, 2026
Joshua Giersch
Trojans women’s soccer players hold up Sophomore Day posters from the bench, during the game against Butte College on Nov. 6.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:16
Instaread

On Nov. 3, Skyline College women’s soccer opened the week with a 1-0 victory over De Anza College, and things got hectic.

The Trojans entered the game with a win-loss record of 5-9. Just days before, they suffered a 3-0 defeat against Feather River College and were looking to bounce back.

Skyline started strong with an impressive unassisted goal by forward Charlie Thelen in the 15th minute. This gave the Trojans the lead for the rest of the game.

Although Skyline was able to maintain their lead for the rest of the first half, things took a turn for the worse in the second half. The Skyline men’s baseball team would show up and all hell would break loose.

The baseball team began energetically supporting the Skyline women’s soccer team with loud cheering, chants and heckling at the referee. It seemed like the Trojans were due for a victory.

But as the cheering and heckling grew more intense, so did the tension between Skyline and De Anza.

In the 74th minute, Skyline defender Azlene Gonzalez dribbled past a De Anza attacker. As Gonzalez nutmegged her, the De Anza player hit her in the face with a closed fist.

This led to an all-out brawl on the field, giving the referee no choice but to hand out red cards to both teams. For Skyline, Gonzalez and attacker Mercy Grech received red cards.

“She (the De Anza player) was pulling me all game,” Gonzalez said. “She kept pulling me, until I cooked her. Then I felt someone hit my face and that’s when I realized it’s serious.”

The altercation escalated to the point where a group of De Anza players surrounded Gonzalez.

“Their whole team went charging at me, at one point it was a six versus one,” Gonzalez said. “They started hitting me, tried to drag me down and started pulling my hair. All of that did nothing, by the way.”

While it may not have caused much physical damage, according to Gonzalez, Skyline head coach Gabe Saucedo said the brawl should not have taken place.

“Unfortunate circumstances, we never want that to happen,” Saucedo said. “We’re always preaching good sportsmanship, so we’ll review the film and learn from this.”

Aside from that, Saucedo was proud of his team’s performance against De Anza.

“I feel good about the victory,” Saucedo said. “We lost to that team in the preseason and we’ve been looking forward to playing them again.”

Skyline went up against Butte College on Nov. 6. The team was looking to turn their recent win into a string of home victories.

It was also their last home game of the season, making it a special game for sophomores Bailey Collins, Charlie Thelen, Daniela Green, Edalene Woolgar, Kristal Alcaraz and Valentina Alarcón Gómez.

“We’re gonna be saying bye to our sophomores,” Saucedo said. “It’s their last home game, we’ll do something special for them, while we try our best to win the game down two players.”

Skyline would lose to Butte College, 3-0. Skyline now has a 6-10 win-loss record and only two games left in their season.

The Skyline College women’s soccer team is set to play against Foothill College on Nov. 10 and West Valley College on Nov. 13.
